Prealgebra · Lesson 12.1

Look for a Pattern

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Some problems are too big to attack head on. Nobody multiplies out the five hundredth term of anything. Instead you compute a few small cases, line the results up, and look for a pattern that repeats. Once you know how it repeats, one short division carries you to the five hundredth case.

Problem
Write out the ones digits of the first several multiples of 88, that is 8,16,24,32,40,48,…8,16,24,32,40,48,…, and watch what the ones digits do. Then predict the ones digit of the 4343rd multiple of 88.
Show a hint
  • The ones digits run 8,6,4,2,08,6,4,2,0 and then start over, a loop of length 55.
  • Divide 4343 by 55 and let the remainder point to a spot inside the loop.
Show the full solution

The ones digits run 8,6,4,2,08,6,4,2,0 and then start over, a loop of length 55. Since 43=8×5+343=8×5+3, the 4343rd multiple sits at the third spot of a fresh loop, so it ends in 44​.

Checking directly, 43×8=34443×8=344.

Problem
A mosaic artist lays tiles along a hallway in a repeating run of nine tiles, five hexagons, then three squares, then one star, over and over. Among the first 500500 tiles, how many are stars?
Show a hint
  • Each full run of 99 tiles contains exactly one star, so first count complete runs inside 500500.
  • Since 500=55×9+5500=55×9+5, there are 5555 full runs plus 55 leftover tiles. Check whether any of those leftovers is a star.
Show the full solution

Dividing, 500=55×9+5500=55×9+5, so the hallway holds 5555 complete runs and then 55 extra tiles.

Each complete run contributes one star, giving 5555 so far. The five leftover tiles are the first five of a new run, all hexagons, so none of them is a star.

55+0=5555+0=55​

Problem
Compute the ones digit of each of 31,32,33,34,3531,32,33,34,35, and keep going just far enough to see the ones digits repeat. How many steps long is the repeating loop?
Show a hint
  • The powers begin 3,9,27,81,2433,9,27,81,243. Read off just the ones digits.
Show the full solution

The ones digits run 3,9,7,13,9,7,1, and then 35=24335=243 brings the digit back to 33, and the loop restarts.

The loop is 3,9,7,13,9,7,1, which is 44​ steps long.

Problem
Using the loop you just found, determine the ones digit of 343343.
Show a hint
  • The loop 3,9,7,13,9,7,1 restarts every 44 powers, so divide 4343 by 44.
  • A remainder of 33 lands on the third digit of the loop.
Show the full solution

Since 43=10×4+343=10×4+3, the exponent 4343 lands three steps into a fresh loop of 3,9,7,13,9,7,1, and the third digit of that loop is 77​.

The exponent could be in the millions and the work would not change, one division by the loop length.

Problem
The powers of 77 have their own ones-digit loop. Find it, then find the ones digit of 7777.
Show a hint
  • Compute ones digits of 71,72,73,7471,72,73,74. Multiplying ones digits only, 7,9,3,17,9,3,1, then the loop restarts.
  • With a loop of length 44, the exponent 77 leaves remainder 33, the third spot.
Show the full solution

Tracking only ones digits, 7×77×7 ends in 99, then 9×79×7 ends in 33, then 3×73×7 ends in 11, and the loop 7,9,3,17,9,3,1 restarts.

Since 7=1×4+37=1×4+3, the seventh power lands on the loop's third digit.

77 ends in 377 ends in 3​

Indeed 77=823,54377=823,543.

Key idea
Find the loop, then use the remainder. Many patterns repeat every kk steps, and the repeating block is called a loop. To track the ones digit of growing powers, keep only the ones digit of each number and drop the rest. A loop has to appear, because there are only ten possible ones digits, so one must eventually repeat. Once you have the loop, divide the target position by the loop length kk. The quotient counts finished loops. The remainder gives the position inside the current loop, with remainder 11 at the first place, remainder 22 at the second, and remainder 00 at the last place.
Problem
A vineyard climbs a hillside in terraces. The top terrace holds 1414 vines, and each terrace below holds 33 more vines than the one above it. How many vines grow on the 2020th terrace from the top?
Show a hint
  • Make a tiny table. Terrace 11 has 1414, terrace 22 has 1717, terrace 33 has 2020. Each step down adds one 33.
  • Reaching terrace 2020 takes 1919 steps down from the top.
Show the full solution

Each terrace adds 33, and getting from terrace 11 to terrace 2020 takes 1919 such steps.

14+19×3=14+57=7114+19×3=14+57=71​

In general the nnth terrace holds the starting 1414 plus n−1n−1 copies of the step.

Problem
How many vines grow on the hillside in total, across all 2020 terraces?
Show a hint
  • Pair the terraces from the outside in. The first with the last gives 14+71=8514+71=85, the second with the second to last gives 17+68=8517+68=85 again.
  • Twenty terraces form 1010 such pairs.
Show the full solution

Pair the top terrace with the bottom one, the second with the second from the bottom, and so on. Every pair totals the same amount,

14+71=17+68=⋯=8514+71=17+68=⋯=85

because each step inward adds 33 to one partner and removes 33 from the other. Ten pairs at 8585 apiece give

10×85=85010×85=850​

Key idea
Build a small table, guess the rule, then check it. Compute the first few values and list them beside their positions. If each step up is the same size, the nnth value is the start plus n−1n−1 steps. To add many of them, pair the first with the last and work inward. Every pair has the same sum. A guessed rule is still a guess. Test it on a case you did not use to build it, or find the reason it works, before using it at position five hundred.
Problem
A fidget counter shows 33. Every button press changes the number by one rule. If the number is even, it is cut in half. If it is odd, 55 is added. So the display reads 3,8,4,2,…3,8,4,2,… as presses go by. What number shows after the 9999th press, that is, as the 100100th number in the list counting the starting 33?
Show a hint
  • Keep pressing. The list runs 3,8,4,2,1,63,8,4,2,1,6 and then returns to 33, so it loops every 66 numbers.
  • Since 100=16×6+4100=16×6+4, the 100100th number sits at the fourth spot of the loop.
Show the full solution

Following the rule, 3→8→4→2→1→6→33→8→4→2→1→6→3, and the display is trapped in a loop of six numbers, 3,8,4,2,1,63,8,4,2,1,6.

With 100=16×6+4100=16×6+4, the 100100th number is the fourth member of the loop.

22​

Iteration problems almost always fall into a loop, because a rule with limited outputs must eventually revisit a number, and from there history repeats exactly.

Problem
A drummer warms up in bursts. The first burst is 11 beat, the second is 33 beats, the third is 55 beats, each burst two beats longer than the last. Compute the total beats after one burst, after two, after three, and after four, and stare at those totals. Then find the total number of beats after the 2020th burst.
Show a hint
  • The running totals are 1,4,9,16,…1,4,9,16,…, which are perfect squares.
  • After nn bursts the total is n2n2, so evaluate 202202.
Show the full solution

The running totals are 1,4,9,161,4,9,16, the perfect squares, so nn bursts should total n2n2 beats. A fifth case agrees, 16+9=2516+9=25.

202=400202=400​

Each new odd burst adds one more L-shaped shell to a square of dots, which grows it to the next square. The next insight draws it.

Key idea
Some patterns add up to squares. The sum 1+3+5+⋯1+3+5+⋯ of the first nn odd numbers is always n2n2, and the picture explains why. Start with one dot. Adding 33 dots in an L shape makes a 2×22×2 square, and adding 55 more makes 3×33×3. Each next odd number is the L-shaped layer needed to reach the next square. Trust a pattern only when you have a reason like this for why it continues.
Fun fact
Patterns without reasons can mislead you. Place dots on a circle and connect every pair. The regions inside count 1,2,4,8,161,2,4,8,16, and nearly everyone bets the sixth dot gives 3232. It gives 3131. The pattern was just a coincidence, which is why solvers always hunt for the why.
Problem
Two neon signs are switched on at the same moment. One flashes every 66 seconds, the other every 1010 seconds. Over the next 33 minutes after switch-on, how many more times will the two signs flash at exactly the same moment?
Show a hint
  • The joint flashes are themselves a repeating pattern. They happen at times that are multiples of both 66 and 1010, and the first is at the least common multiple.
  • Shared flashes come every 3030 seconds, and 33 minutes holds 180180 seconds.
Show the full solution

A shared flash needs a time that is a multiple of 66 and of 1010 at once, and the smallest is lcm(6,10)=30lcm(6,10)=30. So the signs align every 3030 seconds, at 30,60,90,120,150,30,60,90,120,150, and 180180 seconds.

180÷30=6180÷30=6​

Two separate rhythms always merge into one bigger rhythm, and its length is their least common multiple, which you met back in the divisibility chapter.

Key idea
How to find and justify a pattern. Every problem in this lesson used the same four steps. Compute small cases, arrange them in a list or table, state the rule you see, then find the reason it must continue. From there, remainders give the position inside a loop, equal steps and pairing give the sum of a growing list, and a least common multiple gives the first point where two cycles line up.

Practice these ideas

Practice
A road-trip playlist of 88 songs plays on repeat without shuffle. Counting from the first play, which song number is the 7575th song played?
Show the solution

Since 75=9×8+375=9×8+3, nine full passes finish and the 7575th play is the third song of the next pass, song 33​.

Practice
A scarf is knitted in a repeating band of 1212 rows, 55 blue rows followed by 77 white rows. Among the first 400400 rows, how many are blue?
Show the solution

There are 3333 complete bands, each with 55 blue rows, for 165165. The 44 leftover rows are the start of a new band, and the first 55 rows of any band are blue, so all 44 leftovers are blue.

165+4=169165+4=169​

Practice
What is the ones digit of 955955?
Show the solution

Odd powers of 99 end in 99 and even powers end in 11. Since 5555 is odd, 955955 ends in 99​.

Practice
What is the ones digit of 41004100?
Show the solution

The ones digit alternates, 44 for odd exponents and 66 for even ones. The exponent 100100 is even, so the digit is 66​.

Practice
A charm bracelet design puts 77 charms on the first strand, and every following strand carries 44 more charms than the one before. How many charms are on the 1515th strand?
Show the solution

Fourteen steps of 44 sit between the first and fifteenth strands,

7+14×4=7+56=637+14×4=7+56=63​

Practice
A brick staircase has 3030 rows. The top row uses 55 bricks, and each row below uses 22 more bricks than the row above. How many bricks does the whole staircase use?
Show the solution

The bottom row holds 5+29×2=635+29×2=63 bricks. Pairing the top row with the bottom, the second with the second from the bottom, and so on gives 1515 pairs, each totaling 6868.

15×68=102015×68=1020​

Practice
A game screen starts at 66 and updates with every tap. If the number on screen is less than 2020, it doubles. Otherwise, 1515 is subtracted. Counting the starting 66 as the first number, what is the 5050th number to appear?
Show the solution

The screen cycles through 6,12,24,9,18,36,216,12,24,9,18,36,21 and then repeats, a loop of length 77.

Since 50=7×7+150=7×7+1, the 5050th number is the first member of the loop, 66​.

Practice
Adding consecutive odd numbers starting from 11, a student reaches a total of exactly 225225. How many odd numbers did the student add?
Show the solution

The running totals of odd numbers are the perfect squares, so the student stopped when n2=225n2=225, that is n=15n=15​.

Practice
Two meshed gears have 88 teeth and 1414 teeth, and a paint mark sits where they currently touch. As they spin, the marks meet again only after a whole number of teeth have passed on both gears. How many full turns does the small gear make before the two marks first line up again?
Show the solution

The meeting point must be a multiple of both 88 and 1414, and lcm(8,14)=56lcm(8,14)=56 teeth. The small gear completes

56÷8=756÷8=7​

full turns. The big gear makes 44, and the two marks line up again.

Practice
Using the ones-digit loops of 33 and 77, find the ones digit of 343+743343+743.
Show the solution

Both loops have length 44, and 4343 leaves remainder 33, landing on the third spot of each. So 343343 ends in 77 and 743743 ends in 33.

Then 7+3=107+3=10, so the sum ends in 00​.
